summary.headline: Q4 FY26 revenue rose 18% YoY to a record quarter on ~16% volume growth; EBITDA margin held near 27% before VAM-driven price hikes.
summary.overview: Management reported Q4 FY26 revenue up 18% YoY on nearly 16% volume growth, the highest quarterly revenue in company history, with EBITDA margin steady at about 27%. FY26 volume growth was about 8% against 11% in FY25. Raw material VAM prices roughly doubled (management cited INR 80-75 earlier versus INR 160-180 now), and the company has passed through about 60-70% of the increase via price hikes effective early April and 1 May, with a further hike from around 15 May. Management declined to give explicit FY27 guidance, but said it aims for 15-20% volume growth to reach INR 500 crore revenue in two to three years. Receivable days rose to about 150-160 days, which management attributes to new-state dealer build-out and expects to normalise over two to three quarters.

segments.name: Retail / carpenter channel (B2C)
segments.commentary: Retail carpenter-led model covers 14 states via 54 branches, with receivables spread across ~12,000 retailers; overdue per dealer reportedly not above INR 1-2 lakh. Market share cited at ~20% in Maharashtra and 30-35% in Gujarat.

segments.name: OEM
segments.commentary: OEM business started around 2020 and is about 6% of revenue; management is onboarding talent to scale it in metro markets with four OEM product categories.

guidance_outlook: No explicit FY27 volume or revenue number given; board decided not to disclose; management aims for 15-20% volume growth and said clarity may come with the Q2 / nine-month update.

Target of INR 500 crore revenue within two to three years, requiring ~18-20% annual growth per an analyst's calculation; management said this is achievable and later referenced INR 1,000-1,200 crore as a doable long-term aspiration.
Long-term EBITDA margin band of 23-25% (also referenced as 20-25%) to be sustained; gross margin aim of ~65%, but Q1 FY27 expected to be hit by VAM cost increases.
Management expects receivable days to normalise to ~120 within two to three quarters, and about two years for new states to stabilise.
Expects a further price increase around mid-May; says VAM price rise is largely priced in, with stabilisation possibly within about three months if geopolitical conditions ease.
Capacity from 2,000 to 3,500 tonnes per month after brownfield expansion completes in one to two quarters, implying INR 600-650 crore revenue potential.
capex_capacity: Operating at ~65% utilisation on ~2,000 tonnes per month capacity; ~80% of brownfield expansion done, to be completed in one to two quarters, lifting capacity to 3,500 tonnes per month.
March 2026 output crossed 2,100 tonnes per month; management wants capacity ahead of demand to avoid losing share.
Greenfield expansion is planned and to be funded from internal accruals; no amount or timeline given on the call.
New state operations in Odisha and Chhattisgarh to commence in May 2026; Chennai, Kerala and Jammu & Kashmir not yet entered.
Plans to expand into additional major metro markets through OEM distribution.
demand_pricing: VAM is the key raw material, imported and crude-linked; price rose from ~INR 75-80 to ~INR 160-180, and management says VAM is roughly 90% of raw material cost.

Price hikes: management says 60-70% of raw material increase has been passed on, with increases from early April and 1 May and a further one around 15 May; peers took 4-5% in April and ~10% from 1 May.
Adhesives account for ~5-10% of furniture cost (e.g., INR 50,000-1 lakh on INR 10 lakh furniture).
April 2026 volume described as good, partly because dealers stocked ahead of the May price increase; management declined to give an April number.
Management says the West Asia conflict and LPG shortage caused some carpenter migration, though impact described as limited to one or two months; Q4 volumes held up.

Brand: Pankaj Tripathi retained as ambassador; JioHotstar ICC T20 World Cup ATL campaign in Q4. Management says it is 'at par' with the market leader on price after hikes, with sales promotion discounts used to attract dealers.
Loyalty programme: ~2 lakh carpenters registered out of ~3.5 lakh cumulative; ~60% active; target 2.5 lakh by year-end and 3 lakh within 2-3 years.

qa_highlights.question: What volume guidance for FY27 given the capacity additions?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the board decided not to give specific numbers; it aims for 15-20% growth and will update with nine-month results in Q2.

qa_highlights.question: How has raw material (VAM) behaved and how are April and May trending?
qa_highlights.answer: VAM is crude-linked and price roughly doubled; 60-70% of the increase is being passed through, with the 1 May hike effective from the start of May and a further hike around 15 May. Normalisation could take about three months if the situation stabilises.

qa_highlights.question: Advertising spend plan for FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: Advertising and trade marketing was ~4% of revenue (INR 50-54 crore); target is 6-7% for at least three years, with 70-80% in trade marketing and 20-25% in brand communication.

qa_highlights.question: Why are receivables rising and when will they normalise?
qa_highlights.answer: New states need two to three years of dealer engagement; receivable days were ~150-160 against ~120 in FY24-25; management expects control within two to three quarters, with ~1% bad debts historically.

qa_highlights.question: Why hold a large FD / liquid balance rather than pay higher dividends or buy back?
qa_highlights.answer: Management says it has paid 15% of PAT as dividend for six years and retains cash for expansion and market share gains; liabilities of INR 90-95 crore are also tied to the carpenter loyalty programme.

qa_highlights.question: Is demand weakening from price hikes, and how does the furniture-cost share affect demand?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said uptake is normal with some carpenter migration for about one to two months; adhesives are 5-10% of furniture cost, and redemptions remain high.

risks_watch: VAM price volatility and the pace of pass-through; Q1 FY27 margin pressure as B2C pricing lags, with management saying Q1 EBITDA will be affected.
Receivable days at ~150-160 versus ~120 target; watch whether they fall within two to three quarters.
Demand response to 60-70% price hikes and any carpenter migration from LPG shortages in Rajasthan and UP.
Competitive response from larger peers and new capacity in Gujarat (Jivanjor cited by an analyst; management declined to comment).
Greenfield capex size and timing undisclosed; brownfield completion expected in one to two quarters.
Loyalty liability (INR 90-95 crore) redemption pattern; management says FY26 provision-redemption gap was only ~INR 4 crore.
summary.management_tone: Confident on Q4 execution and long-term targets, but cautious and often evasive on FY27 numbers, citing geopolitical uncertainty and declining to give volume, state-wise and April figures. Management repeatedly deferred specifics to the Q2 update or the IR team.
